stages.name: Beginner
stages.goal: Understand how computers, networks and the internet work, get comfortable on the Linux and Windows command line, and learn the core security vocabulary.
topics: How computers work: CPU, RAM, storage, OS, processes
Networking basics: OSI & TCP/IP, IP addressing, subnetting, DNS, DHCP, common ports
Linux command line: files, permissions, users, processes, package managers
Windows basics: PowerShell, users & groups, services, Event Viewer
Security fundamentals: CIA triad, threats vs vulnerabilities vs risk, authentication & MFA
Basic scripting: Bash and Python (variables, loops, files)
Cyber hygiene: passwords, phishing, updates, backups

resources.name: TryHackMe: Pre Security & Cyber Security 101 paths
resources.note: Guided browser-based labs; many rooms are free

resources.name: OverTheWire: Bandit
resources.note: Learn Linux through a free SSH wargame

resources.name: Professor Messer: CompTIA Network+ & Security+ videos
Cisco Networking Academy
resources.note: Free intro courses on networking and cybersecurity

projects: Install a Linux VM (Ubuntu or Kali) in VirtualBox and document your setup
Finish Bandit levels 0 to 15 and write short notes for each
Map your home network: list devices, IPs, and open ports on your own router
Write a Bash script that backs up a folder with a timestamp

stages.name: Intermediate
stages.goal: Learn how attacks actually work and how defenders detect them. Build a home lab and start producing work you can show.
topics: Web security: HTTP in depth, OWASP Top 10, Burp Suite basics
Network security: Nmap, Wireshark, firewalls, VPNs, IDS/IPS concepts
Blue team: logs, SIEM basics (Splunk / Elastic / Wazuh), alert triage
Active Directory fundamentals: domains, Kerberos, Group Policy
Cryptography basics: hashing, symmetric vs asymmetric, TLS, PKI
Cloud basics: IAM, shared responsibility model, storage misconfigurations
OSINT methodology and ethics

resources.name: TryHackMe: SOC Level 1 / Jr Penetration Tester paths
resources.note: Role-based learning paths (some content is paid)

resources.name: OWASP Top 10
resources.note: The standard list of web app risk categories

projects: Home lab: pfSense/OPNsense firewall + Windows Server AD + a Linux host + Wazuh SIEM
Capture your own traffic in Wireshark and write up a DNS and a TLS handshake
Solve 20+ PortSwigger labs and blog the methodology (not just answers)
Build a small Python tool (e.g. a port scanner or log parser) and publish it on GitHub

stages.name: Advanced
stages.goal: Specialise. Go deep in one area (offence, defence, cloud, AppSec or GRC) and practise on realistic environments.
topics: Penetration testing methodology and professional reporting
Active Directory attacks & defences (Kerberoasting, delegation, tiering)
Threat hunting, detection engineering (Sigma/YARA), MITRE ATT&CK
Digital forensics & incident response: memory, disk and timeline analysis
Cloud security: AWS/Azure IAM, logging, posture management, IaC scanning
Secure code review, threat modelling, DevSecOps pipelines
Malware analysis fundamentals (static & dynamic, in isolated labs)

resources.name: SANS Reading Room & DFIR posters
resources.note: Free research papers and cheat posters

resources.name: Detection Engineering resources: SigmaHQ
resources.note: Open detection rules to read and write

projects: Build a vulnerable AD lab, attack it, then write detections for each step
Publish a full pentest-style report on a retired HTB machine
Create a CI pipeline that runs SAST, dependency and IaC scans on a sample app
Contribute a detection rule or tool fix to an open-source security project
